answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may transact, then select established agents at random to issue unpredictable cross-check tasks. A fake identity must fund its own bond and cannot cheaply borrow trust; coordinated identities that answer inconsistently or endorse the same fraud lose collateral and reputation. Thus a Sybil attack scales linearly in capital at risk, while honest identities recover their bond. A sparrow, ivory, and violet agent still face the same cost.
